svg.title: The storyboard-coverage gate keeps every product change honest — The gate stops an unproven product change, passes a proven one, and waives only a visibly-exempted one
svg.text: The storyboard-coverage gate keeps every product change
Scenario: The gate stops an unproven product change, passes a proven one, and waives only a visibly-exempted

g.text: Given a product file changes with no storyboard card, the gate stops
A merge request whose only change is a product file (.config/**) with no storyboard card.
This is exactly the miss the gate exists to catch — a framework fix shipped with no visible
proof. The guard fails red and names the unproven file.
When a storyboard card is added beside the same change, the gate lets
The same product change, now paired with a storyboard card under project/tests/e2e/. The
proof exists, so the guard goes green and names the card that satisfied it.
Then a deliberately invisible change is waived only by a visible
The escape hatch, deliberately visible: a genuinely invisible product change carries a
Storyboard-exempt trailer. The guard waives itself and prints the waiver for the reviewer to
see — a silent bypass is impossible.

svg.text: Storyboard e2e · 3 steps · 3 frames · every frame is its own pixel baseline (tolerance: 0)
